_comment: Featured/curated Overton terms that bypass the podcast mention pipeline. These are pinned at the top of the Overton Window with a 'Debated' badge. Pipeline exports cannot overwrite this file.

featured.thesis: When Treasury doubles long-end liquidity-support buybacks the same week it sells 10s and 30s, the regime is admitting private sponsorship of duration is insufficient without a structural state bid — that is the captive-buyer system around the bond, not a one-off "support" headline. Money is in who warehouses duration (banks/pensions/HTM-SLR/dealer inventory) and the issuer as standing long-end bid while coupon supply continues — not "debt is high," not Nvidia.
featured.who_collects_rent: Whoever sets captivity / balance-sheet rules and runs the buyback backstop — regulators / Treasury / Fed plumbing — not the coupon; dealers take warehouse/fees; equity of stuffed franchises can be leftover.
featured.decisive_test: (1) Sep 9 10y / Sep 10 30y — cover at/above recent averages, no meaningful tail, strong indirects → private bid intact, buyback expansion cosmetic. (2) First enlarged long-end buyback ops after Sep 9 (≥$4bn/op per SB0607 through Nov 4) — thin offers / undersubscribe vs "strong sponsorship" claim → plumbing story overstated. (3) Nov 4 QRA — buyback max sizes cut back or framed temporary → structural state-bid claim fails. (4) 20s30s: Sep 4 par ~−1 bp (20y 5.25 / 30y 5.24); repair via rallying 30y ≠ forced-seller regime.
